motivation: Exploratory cohorts showed repeated 4/5 family slope signs at H=32 versus 5/5 at H=48. This protocol tests a fresh-seed worst-family stability claim without changing the original random-rank metric.
metric: For each width/seed/family, compute target25 minus A_nat 80-20 performance-aligned span at each keep_dim, then OLS slope r_{s,H,f} versus keep_dim. More negative is stronger rank-dependent transfer benefit.
seed_statistic: M_{s,H}=max_f r_{s,H,f}; D_s=M_{s,32}-M_{s,48}. D_s>0 means the narrow H=32 learner has a worse least-stable family than H=48.
primary_pass: D_s > 0 for all 5 fresh seeds; exact one-sided seed sign p=0.03125
stopping: Exactly the five listed seeds; no rescue seeds, width changes, family exclusions, or threshold changes.
interpretation_if_pass: Evidence that learner hidden capacity conditions worst-family stability of the shared-coordinate rank transfer mechanism in this synthetic GRU setup. Does not establish a sharp H=48 threshold, a learner-independent language metric, or natural-language/LLM generality.
interpretation_if_fail: Do not claim confirmed hidden-width conditioning from the exploratory boundary pattern; retain the exploratory result as hypothesis-generating only.
